clips.title: Stop Comparing Yourself To The Best!
clips.content: And the reason for that is often when we want to know if we're doing good, say, how's our social media account doing? Well, we go and find the greatest social media account ever and compare ourselves to it, right? And we're not doing good. But the goal of this is to give a comprehensive view of there are some ministries that are small, and there are some ministries that are large. And you're probably in there somewhere.

clips.title: Is SEO Worth The Time?
clips.content: And one of the things I really like about collecting this type of data is it kind of challenges our assumptions. I regularly talked to ministry leaders who wonder if SEO is even worthier time, because there is cultural biases against religion and that type of thing that are perceived. But the reality is, if people are searching for your content, Google needs to provide results for it.

clips.title: Is your website sending people to social media?
clips.content: So this pie chart here shows that actually 83% of ministries did not have any social media channels listed on their website. And we've seen this as a trend over the last couple of years where people are actually engaging on social media and trying to drive people back to their website rather than push them from their website to social media platforms.

clips.title: You don't need to post every day!
clips.content: The reality is most ministry leaders and digital ministry people don't have the resources to post every day as can be seen. This was also interesting to me because this year, because I was curious as to how AI might affect it,
